comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C116-C117 regarding twofold specificity (cell-type and synapse-type). Both evaluations support these summary claims about the tools' capabilities, though peer reviewers note limited in vivo characterization information.

Perfect agreement on claims C1-C7 establishing background context. Both evaluations support these claims as appropriate background establishing GFE3's prior properties and the rationale for developing new tools.

Both address claims C111-C115 about SAP-102 compensation and knockout mouse phenotypes. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct experimental evidence for C113 and speculative nature of compensation hypothesis. Peer reviewers also express UNCERTAIN, requesting further validation of specificity and broader protein targeting claims.

Both address PSD-95 degradation mechanism (C25-C29). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with appropriate statistics and controls. Peer review R1 includes these claims in broader PFE3 validation, affirming 'convincing demonstration' and 'robust experiments.'

Both address partial PSD-95 degradation and PFE3 design rationale (C32-C37). OpenEval supports claims while noting discrepancy motivating optimization. Peer review includes these in comprehensive PFE3 validation, describing 'engineering, optimization and characterization' as convincing.

Both address PFE3 optimization showing improved PSD-95 reduction (C38-C40, C107-C108). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with strong statistics. Peer review includes these claims in overall PFE3 validation, affirming it as 'major contribution' and 'valuable tool.'

Both address GluA1 reduction and functional connectivity inference (C41-C47). OpenEval supports the calculation and inference as reasonable. Peer review includes these claims, though one reviewer questions whether PFE3 affects additional PSD proteins beyond GluA1.

Both address PFE3 reversibility (C49-C55). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate statistics showing recovery. Peer review includes these claims in PFE3 validation, noting 'reversibility, which is crucial for transient ablation.'

Both address negative controls for PFE3 specificity (C56-C58). OpenEval finds these essential controls SUPPORTED. Peer review includes these in overall validation but raises questions about specificity and impact on inhibitory synapses.

Both address in vivo retinal electrophysiology (C59-C62). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with significant mEPSC reduction. Peer review acknowledges in vivo retinal data but notes 'limited in vivo characterization overall.'

Both address PFE3 molecular architecture (C105-C107). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with experimental validation that all components are necessary. Peer review includes these in comprehensive PFE3 characterization described as 'robust.'

Both address PSD-95 targeting rationale (C21-C24). OpenEval supports the logical progression despite lack of shown data for C23. Peer review includes these claims in PFE3 development narrative without specific concerns.

Partial overlap on PFE3 summary claims (C8, C11-C13). OpenEval R20 addresses all main findings as SUPPORTED. Peer review R1 focuses on PFE3 specifically, affirming it as 'main novelty' and 'valuable tool for neuroscientists.'

Both address PhLIC/paGFE3 design rationale (C63-C67). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer review affirms the tool's effectiveness and praises 'rational design' with low background activity.

Both address PhLIC selection and light-dependent translocation (C68-C74). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate controls. Peer review describes validation as 'robust experiments' with effective spatiotemporal control.

Both address paGFE3 dual function and comparison to Cry2 (C75-C79). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, highlighting advantage over existing systems. Peer review explicitly praises low background activity and rational design.

Both address paGFE3 photobleaching controls (C80-C83). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate controls distinguishing degradation from photobleaching. Peer review includes these in overall 'robust experiments' validation.

Both address paGFE3 time-course and reversibility (C84-C89). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate statistics. Peer review highlights 'reversibility, which is crucial for transient ablation' as key feature.
Partial overlap on paGFE3/chGFE3 summary claims (C9, C14-C19). OpenEval addresses all main findings as SUPPORTED. Peer review affirms tools provide 'spatiotemporal control' with 'robust validation.'

Both address chGFE3 chemogenetic system design (C90-C93). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate citation. Peer review affirms chGFE3 provides spatiotemporal control and is part of 'rational design and robust validation.'

Both address chGFE3 dose-dependent degradation (C94-C97). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with strong statistics and negative controls. Peer review describes 'robust experiments demonstrating reductions in synaptic markers.'

Both address chGFE3 reversibility (C98-C104). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate statistics and functional recovery evidence. Peer review confirms 'reversibility, which is crucial for transient ablation.'

Partial overlap on chGFE3 summary claims (C10, C20). OpenEval addresses all main findings as SUPPORTED. Peer review affirms chGFE3 as part of tools enabling 'selective and efficient synapse ablation.'
OpenEval R22 addresses PSD-95.FingR properties (C30-C31) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific background claims.
OpenEval R23 addresses PSD-95 turnover rate (C48) as SUPPORTED with citation, providing rationale for reversibility experiments. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific claim.
